s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution
salient_findings: Macular edema resolution after intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Hyperreflective tissues proliferating on retinal vessels on OCTA
Dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography
key_facts: 76-year-old woman presented with macular edema
Treated with 2 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Macular edema completely resolved at 3 months
No recurrence of macular edema
OCTA findings at 6 months showed no abnormality
OCTA findings at 12 months showed hyperreflective tissues on retinal vessels
OCTA findings at 15 months showed increased hyperreflective tissues with angiogenic sprouts
OCTA findings at 18 months showed development in area of preexisting proliferation
OCTA findings at 21 months showed enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface
Fluorescein Angiography at 21 months showed dendritic vascular-like structures

shortlist.label: Choroidal neovascularization
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts on OCTA

shortlist.label: Retinal angiomatous proliferation
shortlist.why_kept: Sequential development of proliferations on retinal vessels

shortlist.label: Coats disease
shortlist.why_kept: Dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography

shortlist.label: Retinal telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface on OCTA

shortlist.label: Eales disease
shortlist.why_kept: Retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution

shortlist.label: Idiopathic juxtafoveolar retinal telangiectasis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperreflective tissues on retinal vessels with angiogenic sprouts

shortlist.label: Retinal capillary hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible association with retinal vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
shortlist.why_kept: Possible association with retinal capillary hemangioblastoma

raw.rationale: The patient's OCTA findings showing hyperreflective tissues starting to proliferate on retinal vessels, increased hyperreflective tissues with angiogenic sprouts, and development in the area of preexisting proliferation are consistent with retinal angiomatous proliferation, a type of neovascularization that originates from the retina.

rejected.label: Choroidal neovascularization
rejected.why: The OCTA findings suggest retinal origin of the neovascularization, rather than choroidal origin

rejected.label: Coats disease
rejected.why: Typically presents in young males, and the patient's age and sex do not match

rejected.label: Retinal telangiectasia
rejected.why: The patient's findings are more suggestive of a proliferative process, rather than telangiectasia

rejected.label: Eales disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with retinal vasculitis and peripheral neovascularization, which is not described in the case

rejected.label: Idiopathic juxtafoveolar retinal telangiectasis
rejected.why: The patient's findings are more suggestive of a proliferative process, rather than telangiectasia, and the location is not limited to the juxtafoveolar area

rejected.label: Retinal capillary hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: The patient's findings do not suggest a discrete tumor, and the presence of angiogenic sprouts is not typical of hemangioblastoma

rejected.label: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
rejected.why: The patient's findings do not suggest a systemic disease or a family history of Von Hippel-Lindau disease
